inputs.source: Employee question in SSO authenticated chat
Published HR policy documents maintained by HR content team

controls.name: Read-only least-privilege credential scoped to the policy index
Replies are bound to the authenticated requester's chat session only
Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
Network egress denied at the network layer
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay with model capability because outbound network destinations are blocked outside the model.

controls.name: Model is pinned and changes require a change ticket
Two-person review for publishing policy documents
Prompt limits answers to published Acme HR policies and to saying when policy is silent
controls.decay_rationale: Instruction following is behavioral and can be bypassed by stronger goal manipulation or longer context rationalization.

findings.title: Trusted employee question can elicit internal policy content in the bound chat reply path

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee asks a policy question
Agent reads internal published HR policy content
Agent returns the answer only to the same authenticated requester's chat session

forecast.watch_signal: Chat routing or recipient-binding config diff, new outbound tool or channel in the manifest, or model/version change despite the pinned-model process.

evidence.observation: The agent is limited to answering questions about published Acme HR policies and should use policy_search to find and quote relevant policy.
The only declared tool is policy_search.search, which searches the published HR policy index.

The policy index contains only published policies with internal sensitivity, the agent credential is read-only and scoped to that index, and replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session.
The chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links, and the agent has no other tools, memory, or network egress.

recommendations.action: Keep recipient binding to the authenticated requester's session as a reviewed platform control and require reassessment if any reply destination, forwarding, or sharing feature is added.

findings.title: Policy document poisoning is constrained to internally published content and cannot exfiltrate beyond the asking employee's session

attack_path.note: HR-maintained published policy documents enter the searchable index
Quoted policy content is returned only in the authenticated employee chat session

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion from published policy docs to broader HR sources, weakening of publishing review, or prompt/product change beyond published policy Q&A.

evidence.observation: The policy index holds only published policies, only the HR content team can write to it, and publishing requires two-person review.
The agent is instructed to answer from published policies and to say when policy does not answer the question.
Replies are restricted to the authenticated requester's chat session and the agent has no network egress.

recommendations.action: Maintain the published-policy-only corpus boundary and two-person publishing review; reassess before adding draft, case, or employee-specific HR data sources.

rating.rationale: Manual validation against the schema and checklist was applied because scripts could not run. Based on the declared design, present risk is low because the only tool is a read-only search over internal published policies and the only output path is structurally bound to the authenticated requester's chat session, with network egress denied and verified by pen test. Forecast rises to moderate if recipient binding or corpus boundaries are changed, or if new outbound channels are added, because those changes would remove the structural constraints that currently keep disclosure limited. This assessment reflects declared design and configuration, not observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration supplied in the artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, IaC, or live runtime configuration was provided, so control verification is limited to the statements in the runtime notes except where the notes explicitly say a pen test verified network egress denial.
No protocol manifests beyond the single tool manifest were provided; confidence would increase with runtime-enforced chat recipient-binding evidence and credential policy artifacts.
